S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, either directly, as a witness, or through certain forms of indirect exposure. It is characterized by a pattern of intrusive re-experiencing of the trauma, avoidance of reminders, negative changes in cognition and mood, and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity, persisting for more than one month and causing significant distress or functional impairment. The clinical course can be acute or chronic, with onset sometimes delayed, and symptoms often fluctuating in intensity in response to triggers or life stress. PTSD is distinguished from other anxiety and mood disorders by the requirement of a qualifying traumatic event and the specific pattern of trauma-linked re-experiencing and avoidance.

patient.stressor: Four and a half months ago, on his way back from an early-morning run along the Salish Sea, Sigfredo was riding in a friend's car when they were struck at high speed by a drunk driver who ran a red light on the outskirts of Blaine. His friend in the driver’s seat was critically injured and trapped in the vehicle, and Sigfredo was stuck next to him for several minutes until first responders arrived, witnessing frantic efforts to stabilize his friend and the chaotic scene around them. Initially, Sigfredo focused on being "practical"—helping his parents with insurance calls, keeping his job at the telecom company, and visiting his friend in rehab—while downplaying how shaken he felt, especially in front of his close-knit family and church community. Over the next four months, however, the impact crept into his work, as he started avoiding driving, turning down weekend hikes that required highway travel, and struggling to stay present on customer calls, until his supervisor gently suggested employee counseling after noticing his frequent schedule changes and he agreed to see a mental health provider at the community clinic.
patient.chief_complaint: “Ever since the car crash, it’s like the accident keeps replaying in my head when I’m awake and when I’m trying to relax, and I can’t shut it off.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I’ll lay there staring at the ceiling for hours, and when I finally do knock out I jerk awake over and over from these half-dreams about screeching brakes, so I never feel rested when my alarm goes off for work.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Out of nowhere, like when a customer raises their voice or I hear tires on the wet road outside the call center, it’s like I’m back in the smashed car again hearing my friend gasping and the metal crunching, and I can’t make the scene stop playing in my head no matter how hard I try to think about something else.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I make excuses to my parents and buddies so I don’t have to get in a car or go anywhere near that intersection, and if a conversation even starts drifting toward the accident I shut down or change the subject because I feel like I’ll lose it if I let myself really think about it.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: Since the crash I keep thinking, like, the world’s just not safe and I’m dumb for ever feeling relaxed, and part of me believes if I’d done something different that morning my friend wouldn’t be messed up now, so I must be a screw-up too.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).
S074.manifestation: Most of the time I walk around with this mix of tension and guilt in my chest, like I’m stuck on edge and low-key angry or scared, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or hanging out at church and nothing bad is actually happening.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: I get set off way quicker now, like if a caller starts complaining or my little brother forgets to do the dishes I’ll snap and raise my voice before I even realize I’m doing it, and then I feel bad afterward because that’s not how I used to be.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.
S078.manifestation: On the nights when my head won’t shut up about the crash, I’ll drive way too fast on the back roads or down a couple extra beers at my cousin’s place, kind of not caring if something happens to me, just to feel anything besides this constant knot inside.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Lately I’ve been swapping shifts, calling out more, and getting written up for my call times because I zone out or have to step away, and I’ve also started bailing on church groups and weekend plans with my friends because I just can’t handle being around people or anywhere near cars for long.
add_requirements.duration: All of this—my head replaying the crash, avoiding driving, and feeling on edge—has been going on pretty much since a few weeks after the accident about four and a half months ago and has just stuck with me these past four months.
